## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Kammakathā* ("Discussion of Deeds") is the seventh treatise of the first division (*Mahāvagga*) of the *Paṭisambhidāmagga* [SuttaCentral; Frauwallner 1995]. In his overview of early Abhidharma literature, Erich Frauwallner evaluated the *Kammakathā* (I, 7)—along with the *Abhisamayakathā* (III, 3)—as an isolated attempt within the scholastic tradition to treat a doctrinal problem independently, though he critically observed that such treatments showed little development beyond pedantic elaboration and suggested an Abhidharma tradition that was "silting up and dessicating" [Frauwallner 1995].

No early cross-language parallels are recorded on SuttaCentral or detected by DharmaNexus [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. However, DharmaNexus records widespread Pali-internal text reuse, with 222 matching segments shared across 15 Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. These correspondences include canonical Abhidhamma treatises such as the *Khandhavibhaṅga* (Vb 1), the *Ñāṇavibhaṅga* (Vb 16), and the *Puggalakathā* of the *Kathāvatthu* (Kv 1.1), as well as Nikāya sections from the *Tikanipāta* (AN 3) and *Catukkanipāta* (AN 4) [DharmaNexus]. Extensive textual alignments are also found with later commentarial and sub-commentarial literature, notably the *Abhidhammamātikāpāḷi*, the *Paṭisambhidāmagga-aṭṭhakathā*, the *Dukanipāta-aṭṭhakathā* and *ṭīkā* to the *Aṅguttaranikāya*, and the *Vibhaṅga-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus]. Four modern translations are indexed on SuttaCentral [SuttaCentral].
